interfaces.name: Release application write/read contract
interfaces.invariant: deliveries retains ordinary semantics; fileMedia contains path-only values; server owns FILE metadata

interfaces.name: Unified DeliverySnapshot
interfaces.invariant: itemType, itemKey, filePath and artifactVersion form one valid ordinary or file-media state

interfaces.name: Stable item key
interfaces.invariant: UNIT uses code; FILE uses SHA-256 of the exact trimmed path

interfaces.name: Workflow canonical digest
interfaces.invariant: Stable ordering and content distinguish ordinary version and file path without filesystem access

interfaces.name: Production Entry DTO and history
interfaces.invariant: entryId is tenant-authorized; history partitions by subsystem and itemKey; file version is null

interfaces.name: Analytics summary
interfaces.invariant: ordinary and file-media counts are separate while drilldown remains one row per application

actuators.action: Add append-only V46 with backfill, checks and item-key indexes
actuators.authority: Approved task-scope write access to candidate V46
actuators.impact_radius: Three release-owned tables containing local existing data
actuators.rollback: Before execution remove candidate migration; after execution use verified backup or later compensating migration

actuators.impact_radius: Release application create/update/submit and downstream production input
actuators.rollback: Revert only scoped T1/T2 diffs before file data is retained

actuators.action: Modify production models, Store, service and controller
actuators.impact_radius: Release baseline, result maintenance and production version queries
actuators.rollback: Revert scoped Java only before file production records are retained

disturbances.source: Dirty rokey worktree and user edits
disturbances.effect: Same-file changes can invalidate patches or scope attribution
Duplicate identity can block V46 unique-key migration
V46 version can collide before integration
Real submit or approval flow can fail independent of item implementation
Stale frontend/auth state can produce misleading UI results

delays.sampling_rule: Use focused tests after each task and full tests only at integration gates

delays.source: Flyway DDL and service cold start
delays.consequence: Health sampled too early appears unavailable
delays.sampling_rule: Wait for Started CcbApplication and Flyway V46 log before health probe

delays.consequence: Baseline may not exist until approval event commits
delays.sampling_rule: Poll application status and baseline only after approved lifecycle response
Wait for loading indicators and network requests to settle before DOM/pixel sample

assumptions.text: The isolated local schema is representative for V46.
assumptions.evidence: Current backend uses that schema and Flyway validates through V45.
assumptions.falsifier: Schema introspection or startup differs from migration contracts.

assumptions.text: Stable item key can replace delivery code in all identity paths without changing ordinary semantics.
assumptions.evidence: All identified application, relation and production SQL consumers are in scoped release files.
assumptions.falsifier: Search or tests reveal another unmodeled consumer using delivery code identity.

assumptions.text: Entry-id history can preserve authorization and compatibility.
assumptions.evidence: Controller already has production-version permission and Store can anchor by tenant/id.
assumptions.falsifier: Existing clients require only the old route for file media or route resolution conflicts.

assumptions.text: Frontend associated views are contained in web/src/modules/release.
assumptions.evidence: Repository search found all artifactVersion/deliveries renderers there.
assumptions.falsifier: Runtime or search reveals an external consumer.

control_assessment.action: Use A2/A5 with validation and runtime sensors.
Use A1/A2 and verify Store/runtime facts.
Use bounded compatible actuators and broad regression/security sensors.
Use A5 and required viewport browser measurements.
